privacy.title: Privacy Policy and KVKK Information Notice
privacy.intro: This text is the information notice under Article 10 of Turkish Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK) and Skinora's privacy policy. It explains which personal data we process when you use Skinora, for what purpose and on what legal basis, to whom we transfer it, and what your rights are. We collect only what the service needs; we do not sell personal data and do not use it for advertising.

controller.heading: Data controller
controller.body:
The data controller is Skinora's operator: {legalName}, address: {address}. For any question or request about your personal data, write to {supportEmail}.

If another applicable data protection law (for example the GDPR in the European Union) gives you additional rights, those rights are preserved.

dataWeCollect.heading: Personal data we process
dataWeCollect.body:
- Steam account data: Steam ID, display name, profile picture, the Steam account's creation date and trade eligibility (Mobile Authenticator status, trade hold duration, trade restriction).
- Steam inventory data: the traded item, and item records read from the seller's and the buyer's public inventories during the transaction to verify delivery.
- Your Steam trade link (trade URL).
- Wallet data: the payout and refund addresses you save for each network, your address change history, the address a payment came from, and transaction hashes.
- Transaction data: listings, prices, payments, refunds, cancellations and their reasons, disputes and admin decisions, and the transaction outcomes that make up your reputation score.
- Contact data (optional): your e-mail address, the IDs of the Telegram and Discord accounts you connect, your notification and language preferences.
- Consent records: the date and version of your acceptance of the User Agreement, and the date of your 18+ declaration.
- Technical and security data: your IP address and the country derived from it, the device and browser you sign in with, session records, fraud and security signals (for example the same wallet address being used by more than one account).
- Support correspondence: the e-mails you send us.

We never receive your Steam password, Mobile Authenticator codes, or your wallet's private key or recovery phrase. We do not ask for identity documents; no identity verification (KYC) is performed.

collectionMethod.heading: How we collect data
collectionMethod.body:
- Data received from Steam (Steam OpenID and the Steam Web API) when you sign in with Steam.
- Public inventory and trade eligibility data read through the Steam Web API.
- Data you enter: wallet addresses, trade URL, e-mail, connected accounts, dispute and cancellation descriptions.
- Transfers read from the public blockchains (TRON, Ethereum).
- Records created automatically while you use the site: IP address, device data, session records.

Data is collected electronically, by automated or partly automated means.

purposes.heading: Purposes and legal bases
purposes.body:
Purposes:
- Signing in, managing your account, recording your 18+ declaration and your acceptance of the Agreement.
- Setting up and running transactions: generating the payment address, verifying the payment, verifying delivery from inventories, seller payouts and refunds.
- Handling disputes and support requests.
- Preventing fraud, money laundering and abuse; sanctions screening, geo-blocking and transaction limits.
- Sending notifications through the channels you turn on (in-app, e-mail, Telegram, Discord).
- Keeping the service secure, tracking errors and keeping audit records.
- Meeting legal obligations and answering requests from competent authorities.

Legal bases (processing conditions listed in the KVKK):
- Necessary to conclude and perform the contract: account, transactions, payment, delivery, refunds, disputes and notifications.
- Necessary to fulfil our legal obligations: record keeping, requests from authorities.
- Necessary to establish, exercise or defend a right: disputes, legal claims, audit records.
- Necessary for our legitimate interests, provided your fundamental rights and freedoms are not harmed: fraud prevention, security.
- Made public by you: your public Steam profile and inventory, transfers on the blockchain.

We do not carry out any processing based on explicit consent and we do not send marketing messages.

dataSharing.heading: To whom we transfer data and why
dataSharing.body:
- Valve Corporation (Steam): your Steam ID is sent to Steam for sign-in, inventory and trade eligibility queries.
- Blockchain networks and access providers: payment, payout and refund transfers are written to the public TRON and Ethereum networks; blockchain access (node) providers are used to read the chains and send transfers.
- E-mail delivery service: if you turn on e-mail notifications, your e-mail address and the content of the notification.
- Telegram and Discord: if you connect these channels, notifications are sent to that account's ID.
- Hosting and network security service (Cloudflare): site traffic, including your IP address, passes through this service.
- The other party to a transaction: the data listed in the "What the other party sees" section of the User Agreement.
- Competent public authorities and courts: where there is a legal obligation or a legally valid request.

Some of these providers (Valve, Cloudflare, Telegram, Discord, the e-mail and blockchain access providers) are established outside Türkiye, so the related data is transferred abroad. We do not sell your personal data and do not share it for advertising.

blockchainPublic.heading: Blockchain records
blockchainPublic.body: TRON and Ethereum are public, immutable ledgers. The wallet addresses, amounts and transfer times of your transactions are public on-chain and no one, Skinora included, can delete them. Even if you delete your account the on-chain records remain; Skinora only anonymizes, in its own system, the link between an address and a person.

dataRetention.heading: Retention and deletion
dataRetention.body:
- We keep your data for the service while your account is open. Closing (deactivating) the account does not delete data; the account reopens when you sign in again.
- When you delete your account, your Steam ID is replaced with an anonymous identifier; your display name, profile picture, e-mail address, trade URL, saved wallet addresses, notification channels and session records (including device and IP data) are deleted or anonymized.
- Transaction history and audit records (money movements, address change history, admin decisions, security events) are kept indefinitely after deletion, linked to the anonymized account; they are needed for disputes, accounting, fraud prevention and legal obligations. The wallet addresses and transaction hashes in these records are not deleted, because they are already public on-chain.
- Records subject to a legal retention obligation are kept for as long as that obligation requires.

yourRights.heading: Your rights
yourRights.body:
Under Article 11 of the KVKK you have the right, by applying to the data controller, to:
- learn whether your personal data is processed,
- request information if it has been processed,
- learn the purpose of the processing and whether the data is used in line with that purpose,
- know the third parties in Türkiye or abroad to whom it has been transferred,
- ask for it to be corrected if it is incomplete or inaccurate,
- ask for it to be deleted or destroyed,
- ask for corrections, deletions or destructions to be notified to the third parties it was transferred to,
- object to a result against you that arises from analysis exclusively by automated systems,
- claim compensation if you suffer damage because of unlawful processing.

How to exercise your rights:
- To close or delete your account, use the "Account Management" section of your account settings. Even if you have not accepted the User Agreement, you can close or delete your account from the "I do not accept the terms" option on the acceptance screen. An account cannot be closed or deleted while it has an active transaction.
- For any other request, write to {supportEmail} and include your account's Steam ID. Before acting on a request we verify that the account is yours (for example by asking you to sign in with Steam).
- We answer requests within 30 days at the latest, free of charge.
- If you find our answer insufficient, you can lodge a complaint with the Turkish Personal Data Protection Board (Kişisel Verileri Koruma Kurulu).
- Limit of the deletion right: transaction history and audit records are kept in anonymized form ("Retention and deletion").

security.heading: Security
security.body: We take technical and organisational measures to protect your personal data against unauthorized access, loss and misuse: site traffic is carried over an encrypted connection (HTTPS), the session renewal token is kept in a cookie that browser scripts cannot read, access to internal systems is limited by authorization, and money movements and admin actions are written to an audit log. Skinora never asks for your Steam password or wallet keys; a message asking for them does not come from Skinora.

cookies.heading: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.body:
We only use what the service needs to work:
- Session renewal cookie: keeps you signed in; browser scripts cannot read it.
- Short-lived security cookies during sign-in: protect the return from Steam sign-in.
- Language cookie: remembers the language you chose.
- Browser storage: the session access token and the draft of an unfinished listing form are kept in your browser.

We do not use advertising, analytics or third-party tracking cookies.

minors.heading: Under 18
minors.body: Skinora is not directed at people under 18, and people under 18 cannot open an account. If we learn that someone under 18 has opened an account, we close it and delete the data under the rules in this notice.

changes.heading: Changes to this notice
changes.body: We may update this notice; the current version is published on this page and the date at the top changes. If we are going to process your data for a new purpose, we will tell you separately.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: For any question or request about your personal data: {supportEmail}. The data controller's details are at the bottom of this page.

terms.title: User Agreement
terms.intro:
This User Agreement (the "Agreement") governs the relationship between you and the operator of Skinora ("Skinora", "we"), a platform that holds the buyer's payment in escrow in CS2 item sales. Operator: {legalName}, address: {address}.

After signing in with Steam you accept the 18+ declaration and this Agreement with checkboxes. Without accepting you cannot start or accept a transaction or receive a payout. If you do not want to accept, you can close or delete your account from the same screen. The processing of personal data is described in the Privacy Policy and KVKK Information Notice.

parties.heading: Definitions and language
parties.body:
In this Agreement:
- Seller: the user who starts a transaction to sell a CS2 item.
- Buyer: the user the seller names by Steam ID and who accepts the transaction.
- Transaction: the sale of a single item at a single price.
- Escrow: holding the buyer's payment on a payment address dedicated to that transaction and controlled by Skinora until the conditions in this Agreement are met.
- Network: the blockchain the payment is made on — TRON (USDT TRC-20) or Ethereum (USDT ERC-20).

The Agreement is published in Turkish, English, Spanish and Chinese. The Turkish text is authoritative; if the translations differ in meaning, the Turkish text prevails.

eligibility.heading: Who can use Skinora
eligibility.body:
Only users who meet all of the following can use Skinora:
- Being at least 18 years old and declaring it.
- Not being located in a country where access is blocked (a sanctioned country) and not appearing on any sanctions list. Blocked countries are determined from your IP address; wallet addresses on a sanctions list are not saved.
- Signing in with a Steam account of your own. The Steam account must have reached the minimum account age set by the platform.
- Having Steam Mobile Authenticator turned on (both parties). Accounts with a Steam trade restriction — "limited" accounts that have not spent at least 5 USD, and new accounts in their first 15 days — cannot trade and therefore cannot take part in a transaction.

We do not perform identity verification (KYC). If we find that a condition is not met, we may refuse the service, suspend the account or freeze open transactions ("Suspension, account closure and deletion").

serviceDescription.heading: Nature of the service
serviceDescription.body:
Skinora is an escrow intermediary: the item never passes to Skinora; the only thing held in escrow is the buyer's money. The item goes directly from the seller to the buyer in a single Steam trade; the seller sends the trade offer and Skinora is not a party to that trade. Skinora therefore does not hold or deliver the item and cannot guarantee that the seller will actually send it. What it guarantees is that the buyer's money is refunded when the item is not delivered under the rules of this Agreement.

Skinora does not hold user balances: you send the payment from your own wallet or exchange, and payouts and refunds go to the user's saved address. The seller sets the price; Skinora does not interfere with it and gives no assurance about an item's market value, authenticity or future tradability.

Skinora is an independent service; it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or operated by Valve Corporation or Steam.

transactionFlow.heading: Transaction flow
transactionFlow.body:
Every transaction follows the same order:
1. The seller picks the item from their inventory, enters the price in USDT, chooses the networks they accept (TRON, Ethereum or both) and the payment window, and enters the buyer's Steam ID. Skinora checks that the item is in the seller's inventory and tradable.
2. The buyer reviews the transaction, chooses one of the networks the seller accepts, provides a refund address on that network and their Steam trade link (trade URL), and accepts. No payment is made at this step.
3. The seller confirms they are ready to send the item. Skinora checks the item again and shows the payment address to the buyer only after this confirmation.
4. Within the payment window, the buyer sends the total shown, on the chosen network, in one transfer to the payment address dedicated to that transaction.
5. When the payment is final on the blockchain, Skinora verifies it automatically and tells the seller to send the item.
6. Within the delivery window, the seller sends the item directly to the buyer with a Steam trade offer.
7. Delivery is verified by the buyer's confirmation or by inventory evidence.
8. When the settlement period ends, Skinora takes the commission and sends what the seller is owed to the seller's payout address on that network.

A transaction's item, price and accepted networks cannot be changed after it is created; a seller who wants to change them cancels and opens a new one. Each transaction contains a single item, and the same item cannot be in more than one open transaction at a time. The remaining time of each step is shown on the transaction page; a step whose time runs out cancels the transaction ("Cancellation and withdrawal").

paymentAndNetworks.heading: Payment, network and token
paymentAndNetworks.body:
- The only means of payment is USDT: USDT on TRON (TRC-20) or USDT on Ethereum (ERC-20). No other token or network is accepted.
- A transaction uses a single network: the one the buyer chose. The payment, the payout and every refund are made on that network; there is no moving money between networks, no bridging and no conversion.
- A separate payment address is generated for each transaction. Do not send to an earlier transaction's address.
- Send the total shown in a single transfer and exactly. Skinora does not combine partial payments and applies no tolerance to the amount: a short amount is not accepted and is refunded; the excess of an overpayment is refunded and the transaction continues; transfers arriving after the first correct one are refunded.
- If you send USDC by mistake, it is refunded automatically. A token or contract Skinora does not recognise cannot be refunded automatically; it goes to admin review.
- An Ethereum address also looks valid on other EVM networks. A payment sent from a network other than Ethereum (for example BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum) does not count for the transaction and is not refunded automatically; a support request is needed. Follow the network warning on the payment screen.
- A payment is verified once it is final on the blockchain. A late payment (one that arrives after the payment window has expired) does not reopen the transaction; it is refunded.
- Every refund in this section goes to the refund address the buyer gave for that network at acceptance, minus the refund's network fee ("Refunds").

fees.heading: Fees
fees.body:
- The buyer pays the commission. The commission is a percentage of the price, rounded down to the cent and added to the total due. The rate is fixed for the transaction when it is created; a later change of rate does not affect an open transaction. The applicable amounts are shown before you accept.
- On TRON the buyer also pays a "TRON network fee". This fee is the blockchain cost of moving the payment from the transaction's payment address to Skinora's wallet; it is calculated and fixed at acceptance and added to the total. If the move later turns out more or less expensive, the amount does not change: Skinora covers any shortfall and keeps any surplus. There is no such fee on Ethereum; Skinora covers the cost of the move.
- Network fee of the payout to the seller: on TRON Skinora covers it, but if the fee exceeds a set percentage of the commission (the protection threshold, 10% by default) the excess is deducted from what the seller receives. On Ethereum the seller receives the full price.
- You pay the network fee of sending the payment from your own wallet or exchange, and your exchange's own fees.
- The network fee of a refund is deducted from the refund amount ("Refunds").
- Blockchain network fees are set by the TRON and Ethereum networks; Skinora does not control them.

delivery.heading: Delivery
delivery.body:
- After the payment is verified, the seller has 12 hours to send the item to the buyer (the delivery window). The remaining time is shown on the transaction page and the seller is warned before it runs out.
- The seller sends the trade offer to the trade URL the buyer gave in the transaction; Skinora gives the seller this link ready to use.
- Delivery is verified in one of two ways: the buyer confirms "I received it", or Skinora sees together that the item has left the seller's inventory and that the expected count has increased in the buyer's inventory (inventory evidence). When inventory evidence is seen, the buyer is notified to check and confirm; letting the evidence alone release the payment is a setting Skinora turns on after reviewing the first real deliveries.
- As a buyer, do not confirm "I received it" before you see the item in your Steam inventory: the confirmation opens the way to the seller's payout and cannot be undone.
- If your Steam inventory is private, inventory evidence cannot be produced; delivery is verified only by your confirmation.
- Delivery of an item of the same kind counts as delivery. Wear (float) or pattern differences are not checked automatically; such a difference is handled through a "wrong item" dispute.
- Just before the delivery window ends, Skinora checks one last time; if delivery is seen, the transaction is not cancelled. If it is not, the transaction is cancelled, the buyer's money is refunded and the delay is recorded against the seller.
- Time limits are frozen during Steam outages and platform maintenance and continue from where they stopped once it is over.

settlement.heading: Settlement period and payout to the seller
settlement.body:
- Steam keeps an item that changed hands in a trade reversible for 7 days, and either side of the trade can start the reversal. That is why, after delivery is verified, the seller's payout is held for 8 days (the settlement period); the money stays in escrow during that time.
- At the end of the period, just before paying out, Skinora checks that the item is still in the buyer's inventory. If it is, the commission is taken, the rest is sent to the seller and the transaction completes.
- If the item is no longer with the buyer and has returned to the seller, the trade is treated as reversed: the seller is not paid, the money is refunded to the buyer after admin review, and the seller's account is flagged for fraud.
- If the situation cannot be told apart (the item is not with the buyer, but it does not appear to have returned to the seller either), no automatic decision is made; an admin reviews it and the money waits until a decision is made.
- The payout goes to the payout address fixed for that network when the transaction was created. Changing the address in your profile later does not affect an open transaction.
- If you think you did not receive a payout, report it on the transaction page; the transfer is checked on the blockchain, retried if needed or passed to an admin.
- On each network, payouts to sellers leave from the same Skinora sending address. If you receive the payout at an exchange in Türkiye, your exchange may ask you to declare the sender ("Exchanges in Türkiye and MASAK").

cancellation.heading: Cancellation and withdrawal
cancellation.body:
- Before the payment is sent, both the seller and the buyer can cancel the transaction; no refund is needed because no money has moved.
- Once the buyer has sent the payment, the buyer cannot cancel unilaterally. The seller can cancel by deciding not to send the item; the money is then refunded to the buyer, the seller's reputation drops and the seller is barred from opening new transactions for a period.
- The party who cancels must give a reason. A user who cancels many transactions within a short time is temporarily barred from starting transactions.
- If a step's time runs out, the transaction is cancelled; if the payment has been received, it is refunded to the buyer.
- Skinora admins may cancel active transactions, with a stated reason, before the item is delivered. In high-risk situations (a sanctions match, suspected account takeover) they may temporarily freeze any active transaction; time limits stop during the freeze. Once the item has been delivered, standard cancellation no longer applies; exceptional cases are reviewed manually.

Withdrawal: you can withdraw from a transaction free of charge before sending the payment. When you send the payment, performance of the escrow service begins at your request and with your consent; from that moment the buyer cannot cancel unilaterally and the money is refunded only in the cases written in this Agreement.

refunds.heading: Refunds
refunds.body:
- Refunds are for money only; there is no item refund, because the item is never with Skinora.
- A refund goes to the refund address the buyer gave at acceptance for the chosen network. Refunds of rejected payments (a short amount, the excess of an overpayment, later transfers in a split payment, a wrong token, a payment arriving after the window expired) go to the same address.
- When an accepted payment is refunded, the buyer gets back the price and the commission. The TRON network fee is refunded in full if the refund happens before the payment is moved to Skinora's wallet; if it happens after the move, it is not refunded because it has been spent.
- The network fee of each refund is deducted from the refund amount; the buyer receives "refunded amount − the refund's network fee". The fee is calculated from the blockchain just before sending; if it cannot be calculated, the smaller of the network's fallback fee and the last measured fee is used. The deducted fee is shown in the notification.
- If the network fee would swallow most of the refund (the net refund is less than twice the refund's network fee), the refund is not sent automatically; the money stays on the transaction's payment address and an admin decides manually.
- The buyer is responsible for the refund address being correct. A refund sent to a wrong address, or to one that is not yours, cannot be recovered.

disputes.heading: Disputes
disputes.body:
- Only the buyer opens a dispute. Because payouts to the seller are made automatically, there is no dispute on the seller's side; the seller reports a payout they did not receive on the transaction page.
- Dispute types: payment dispute ("I paid but it does not show"), delivery dispute ("the item did not arrive") and wrong item dispute.
- Automatic checks run first: the payment is looked up on the blockchain, delivery evidence is checked again, and for a wrong item the item that entered the buyer's inventory is compared with the item in the transaction. If the item left the seller but did not reach the buyer, the case goes directly to an admin.
- If the automatic result does not satisfy you, you can escalate the dispute to an admin. The admin decides in the seller's favour (payout to the seller) or in the buyer's favour (refund to the buyer); both parties are notified and the decision is recorded. In a transaction where delivery is proven, the default decision is in the seller's favour; a decision in the buyer's favour requires a separate justification.
- A second dispute of the same type cannot be opened on the same transaction. A dispute does not stop time limits; a transaction whose time runs out is cancelled, the dispute closes and the standard refund rules apply.
- Events Skinora cannot see or prevent, such as Steam confiscating the item, banning the account or changing its trading system, are not resolved through a dispute ("Liability").

userObligations.heading: Your obligations
userObligations.body:
- Use only a Steam account and wallet addresses that are yours and under your control. Enter your payout and refund addresses correctly for each network and read the confirmation step when entering an address.
- Send the payment on the network chosen in the transaction, in the exact amount and in one transfer.
- Complete the trade honestly and on time. As a seller, send the trade offer only to the buyer's trade URL and do not reverse the trade after delivering the item.
- Do not sell stolen or wrongfully obtained items, or items over which someone else has a right.
- Do not attempt fraud, money laundering, getting around the rules with several accounts, or evading sanctions screening or geo-blocking.
- Comply with Steam's terms of use and with applicable law. Tax and similar legal obligations arising from your sales are yours.
- Never share your Steam password, Mobile Authenticator codes, or your wallet's private key or recovery phrase; Skinora never asks for them.

visibility.heading: What the other party sees
visibility.body: In a transaction, the parties see each other's Steam profile (display name, profile picture, Steam ID) and Skinora reputation score. The seller sees the buyer's Steam trade URL so that they can send the trade offer. Because payments and refunds are made on the blockchain, the wallet addresses and transfers of the transaction are public on-chain. Use the other party's data only to complete the transaction.

restrictions.heading: Transaction limits and account security
restrictions.body:
- Skinora applies limits on the minimum and maximum transaction amount, the number of simultaneous active transactions, and the first transactions of new accounts. A transaction that hits a limit is rejected before it is created and the reason is shown.
- Transactions whose price deviates significantly from the market price, or that create a high volume in a short time, are held for admin approval before they start.
- The account of a seller who, after receiving payment, does not deliver, cancels or reverses the trade is first flagged and then suspended if it happens again.
- Changing a payout or refund address requires re-confirmation with Steam; for a period after the change, starting and accepting transactions is blocked. Open transactions complete with the address fixed when they were opened.
- If an address matches a sanctions list, it is not saved, the account is flagged and the account's active transactions are frozen.

masak.heading: Exchanges in Türkiye and MASAK
masak.body:
Crypto-asset service providers (exchanges) in Türkiye, under MASAK regulation, apply a waiting period and amount limits to withdrawals to external wallets and make you declare the other party of a transfer. Your exchange sees Skinora's payment and sending addresses as external wallets. Your exchange applies these rules, not Skinora. Sending the payment on time and in one transfer, and making the declaration correctly, are the user's responsibility. The waiting period, the limits and the declaration details are in the "Exchanges in Türkiye and MASAK rules" section of the Support page; that information is a practical summary, not legal advice.

If the declaration asks for legal-entity details: legal name {legalName}, address {address}.

liability.heading: Liability
liability.body:
Skinora guarantees:
- That payments are verified on the blockchain.
- That the money in escrow is handled according to the flow in this Agreement: held until delivery is verified, passed to the seller once it is, refunded to the buyer if it cannot be.
- That delivery verification follows the written evidence rules, and that a transaction is not closed silently but put under review when evidence cannot be produced.
- That on expiry and cancellation the money is refunded, within the scope of supported assets.

Skinora is not responsible for:
- The item itself: Skinora never holds the item; the consequence of a seller not sending it is the refund of the buyer's money.
- Steam confiscating the item, banning an account, changing its trading system or its outages; an item turning out to be stolen.
- Reversals Steam makes on its own decision. Against a reversal by a party to the trade within the settlement period, Skinora protects by holding the seller's payout ("Settlement period and payout to the seller").
- Unusual events on the TRON or Ethereum network (network outages, extreme fee spikes and the like) and exchanges' own rules or delays.
- User error: sending from the wrong network, with the wrong amount or to the wrong address, a wrongly entered payout or refund address, sharing credentials.

Our obligation to pass the money in escrow to the seller or refund it to the buyer in accordance with this Agreement is not limited. Beyond that, and without prejudice to liability for intent and gross negligence and to liability that cannot be limited by law, Skinora is not liable for indirect losses (loss of profit, loss of an item's value, loss of opportunity).

indemnity.heading: Indemnity
indemnity.body: To the extent permitted by applicable law, you cover the loss Skinora suffers because you breach this Agreement or applicable law (for example by selling a stolen item or attempting fraud), and the claims third parties bring against Skinora for that reason.

suspension.heading: Suspension, account closure and deletion
suspension.body:
- We may flag, suspend or close accounts that breach this Agreement or applicable law, or that trip the fraud or sanctions rules. A suspended account can sign in but cannot take actions that move money; the automatic steps of open transactions continue, and steps that need the user's action are cancelled when their time runs out.
- You can close (deactivate) or delete your account from settings at any time. Even without accepting the terms, you can do the same from the "I do not accept the terms" option on the acceptance screen. An account cannot be closed or deleted while it has an active transaction; the transaction must first complete or be cancelled.
- A closed account reopens when you sign in again. On deletion your personal data is deleted or anonymized; transaction history and audit records are kept in anonymized form (Privacy Policy).
- Money in escrow is handled under this Agreement even if the account is suspended or closed.

changes.heading: Changes
changes.body: We may update this Agreement. The current text is published on this page and the date at the top changes. For a material change, you are asked to accept the new text at your next session. Changes apply to transactions started after they are published; an open transaction completes under the terms in force when it started.

governingLaw.heading: Governing law and jurisdiction
governingLaw.body:
This Agreement is governed by the law of the Republic of Türkiye. The courts and enforcement offices of {courtVenue} have jurisdiction over disputes arising from it. Users acting as consumers keep their right to apply to consumer arbitration committees within the monetary limits set by consumer law, and to consumer courts for disputes above those limits.

Before taking a dispute to court, please bring it to our support address ({supportEmail}); most problems are solved quickly from the transaction records.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: Send questions about this Agreement to {supportEmail}. The operator's details are at the bottom of this page.

support.title: Support
support.intro: Need help with a transaction or your account? This page explains how to reach our team, how long a reply takes, how disputes work and what to watch for when paying from an exchange in Türkiye.

contact.heading: Contact us
contact.body:
You can reach support by e-mailing {supportEmail}. To help us help you faster, include your transaction ID, the transaction's network (TRON or Ethereum), the transaction hash if there is one, and a short description of the problem.

Never share your Steam password, Mobile Authenticator codes, or your wallet's private key or recovery phrase with anyone, including support; Skinora never asks for them.

responseTimes.heading: Response times
responseTimes.body: We aim to reply within one business day and give priority to transactions whose payment is waiting in escrow and whose time is running. This is a target, not a guarantee: during busy periods, Steam outages or blockchain congestion replies are slower. We answer requests about your personal data within 30 days at the latest.

disputes.heading: Transaction disputes
disputes.body:
If a trade does not go as expected, open a dispute from the transaction page:
- The buyer opens it: a payment dispute (I paid but it does not show), a delivery dispute (the item did not arrive) or a wrong item dispute.
- Automatic checks run first; if the result does not satisfy you, you can escalate the dispute to an admin.
- The admin decides in the seller's favour (payout to the seller) or in the buyer's favour (refund to the buyer); both parties are informed.
- A dispute does not stop the delivery window: if it runs out, the transaction is cancelled and the money is refunded to the buyer.
- If you are a seller and did not receive the payout of a completed transaction, report it on the transaction page; the transfer is checked on the blockchain.

Details are in the "Disputes" section of the User Agreement.

masak.heading: Exchanges in Türkiye and MASAK rules
masak.body: Under MASAK regulation, crypto exchanges in Türkiye apply a waiting period and amount limits to withdrawals to external wallets, and make you declare the counterparty of a transfer you send or receive. Your exchange sees Skinora's payment addresses as external wallets. These rules are applied by your exchange, not by Skinora; the summary below is practical information, not legal advice.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.body:
- Which payment method do you accept? Only USDT: on TRON (TRC-20) or on Ethereum (ERC-20). The seller chooses the networks they accept and the buyer picks one of them.
- I sent the payment from the wrong network. A payment sent from an EVM network other than Ethereum (for example BNB Smart Chain, Polygon) does not count for the transaction and is not refunded automatically; write to us with the transaction ID and the transaction hash.
- I sent too little or too much. A short amount is not accepted and is refunded; the excess of an overpayment is refunded and the transaction continues. Refunds go to your refund address minus the refund's network fee.
- How much do I pay? The buyer pays price + commission; on TRON the TRON network fee is added. The total due is shown separately for each network on the acceptance screen.
- When must the seller send the item? Within 12 hours after the payment is verified. If they do not, the transaction is cancelled and your money is refunded.
- I received the item — what now? Once you see the item in your Steam inventory, confirm "I received it" on the transaction page. Do not confirm before you see the item.
- As a seller, when do I get paid? 8 days after delivery is verified, once it is checked that the item is still with the buyer. This wait protects the buyer against Steam's 7-day trade reversal window.
- Why is Steam Mobile Authenticator required? If either party has it turned off, Steam holds the trade for 15 days, so it must be on for both. Steam accounts that have not spent at least 5 USD or are in their first 15 days cannot trade.
- I will pay from an exchange in Türkiye. Exchanges send newly bought USDT to an external wallet no earlier than 48 hours later (72 hours on the first withdrawal) and apply a daily limit; buy the USDT before accepting the transaction. Details are in the MASAK section above.
- How do I delete my account? From Settings > Account Management. If you have not accepted the User Agreement, from the "I do not accept the terms" option on the acceptance screen. An account cannot be deleted while it has an active transaction.
- I got a message asking for my Steam password or wallet keys. Skinora never asks for them; do not reply and let us know.

closures.heading: Outbound row closure (two-person)
closures.intro: Use this only when the Ethereum signing service lost its journal and a payment already went out on-chain while its row still shows pending. One admin proposes the on-chain transaction hash; a different admin approves it by typing the hash again. This tool never sends money.

buyer.title: Paying from an exchange in Türkiye?
buyer.holdInAdvance: Have the USDT in your account in advance: exchanges send crypto you bought, swapped or deposited to an external wallet no earlier than 48 hours later, and at least 72 hours later on your first withdrawal from the exchange. If the payment window is shorter than this wait, newly bought USDT will not arrive in time.
buyer.dailyLimit: Withdrawals of stable-value crypto such as USDT are limited to 3,000 $ a day and 50,000 $ a month (your exchange may apply double in some cases). The limit applies to the daily and monthly TOTAL, not to a single transfer: withdrawals you already made the same day reduce your remaining allowance. If the amount to send is above what is left, you cannot send the payment in one transfer from a Turkish exchange.
buyer.declare: Your exchange asks you to declare the recipient: the recipient is Skinora, the address is this transaction's payment address. Every transaction has a different payment address — do not send to an address you saved for an earlier transaction.
buyer.description: Your exchange asks for a transaction description of at least 20 characters, for example "Skinora CS2 item purchase payment".
buyer.source: Your exchange applies these rules under MASAK regulation, not Skinora. This is a practical summary, not legal advice.
buyer.short: Paying from an exchange in Türkiye? Buy the USDT now: exchanges send newly bought, swapped or deposited crypto to an external wallet no earlier than 48 hours later (72 hours on the first withdrawal) and limit USDT withdrawals to 3,000 $ a day. If the payment window is shorter than this wait, USDT bought later will not arrive in time.

seller.title: Receiving the payout on an exchange in Türkiye?
seller.declare: Your exchange may ask you to declare the sender of the payout from Skinora: the sender is Skinora. Skinora's payouts always leave from the same address on each network; if your exchange keeps your declaration for this address, you can reuse it for later payouts.
seller.addressUnavailable: The sender address cannot be shown right now. When the payout arrives, you can see the sender from the transaction hash.
seller.changeNote: If this address changes, the new address appears here; update the record at your exchange.

help.paymentWindow: The payment window is the time the seller chose in the listing and shows as a countdown on the transaction page. Your exchange's wait can be longer, so buy the USDT before you accept the transaction.
help.refund: Refunds also come from a Skinora address (the transaction's deposit address or the hot wallet). If your refund address is at a Turkish exchange, the exchange may ask you for a sender declaration: the sender is Skinora.
help.sources: Source: MASAK General Communiqué (No. 29), Official Gazette of Türkiye 28.06.2025, issue 32940, article 4; Regulation on Measures Regarding Prevention of Laundering Proceeds of Crime and Financing of Terrorism, article 24/A.
